#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

DEST="backup-srv:/srv/nightly"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command: chmod +x backup.sh; sh -n backup.sh && echo "syntax OK"

text:
I filled in the backup destination as instructed: `backup.sh` now sets `DEST="backup-srv:/srv/nightly"`, tars `logs/` into `logs-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz`, and uses `scp` to copy that tarball to `backup-srv:/srv/nightly/`. `set -eu` is already in place so the script will exit non-zero (and the tarball won't be silently lost) if either the tar or the scp step fails. Verified the script parses cleanly with `sh -n`.

Note: this assumes passwordless/key-based SSH access to `backup-srv` is already configured on the host that runs the cron job — I didn't set up or verify SSH keys, since that's outside this repo's scope. Worth confirming that's in place before tonight's run.
